title: Signal middleware for tracing/metrics pipelines and automated alert de-escalation matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight signal middleware layer that standardizes sampling, enrichment, and downstream routing for traces, metrics, and logs, and combine it with an automated alert de-escalation matrix to reduce pager noise while preserving SLO fidelity.

Context: Our current observability stacks send heterogeneous signals to multiple downstream consumers (SLO pipeline, anomaly detector, latency dashboards, runbooks). Differences in sampling, attribute naming, and routing lead to duplicate alerts, high noise during multi-region incidents, and difficulty attributing true SLO impact to signal-level anomalies. This ticket implements a middleware shim at the ingestion boundary and an explicit de-escalation matrix that codifies when an alert should escalate to paging vs. be handled by a resilient notification channel.

Key responsibilities in this ticket: unify trace/metric/log attributes (request_id, service.owner, route_group), implement per-tenant sampling inheritance, attach KV-cache keys and model-serving context for inference requests, add dynamic routing rules (anomaly->postprocess, SLO->aggregator, dashboard->raw-index), and wire an alert de-escalation policy engine that factors signal confidence, correlated signals, deploy window, and burn-rate contribution before triggering paging.

Trade-offs considered:
- Centralized enrichment increases latency at the ingestion edge; mitigated by async enrichment workers and short-circuit fast-paths for high-priority signals.
- More aggressive sampling reduces cost but may harm SLO attribution; we'll use adaptive sampling controlled by SLO impact heuristics.
- Policy complexity vs. transparency: we will store decision logs for every alert decision to allow oncall review and replay.

Deliverables:
- Middleware service (go/rust) with k8s helm chart and canary routing.
- Policy engine with JSON rule format, UI hooks for Console team to surface de-escalation state.
- Integration adapters for SLO aggregator, anomaly detector, and latency dashboards.
- Runbook additions and playbook for testing noisy degradation scenarios.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ingestion path latency P99 increase <= 8ms on canary traffic for fast-path signals.
- Duplicate alert rate reduced by >= 40% for week-long baseline in staging.
- SLO attribution accuracy (recall of true SLO-affecting incidents) >= 95% in controlled chaos test.
- Decision logs available and queryable from Console within 30s of decision.

Rollout plan: deploy to staging -> 10% capacity canary on dedicated infra -> synthetic workload + chaos testing -> 50% regional traffic for 24h -> full rollout. Backoff policy: automated disable if SLO aggregator lag > 2m or duplicate alert surge > 10%.

Notes on implementation: favor Rust service for lower tail latency, use protobuf for internal wire format to maintain schema evolution, and expose a minimal HTTP health/status + /decision-log endpoint for Console integration. Use feature flags to gate policy engine.
